quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #22
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If you see heavy smoke ahead on the road, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on your four-way flashers and keep driving.
Slow down, move to the right, and stop off the road.
Turn on your high beam headlights and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to the right, and stop off the road.
questions.explanation: If you see heavy smoke ahead, slow down right away. Move as far right as possible and stop off the road. Then decide if it is safe to continue. Some smoke can harm your eyes, lungs, or be deadly.

questions.question: You and the driver on your left reach a four-way stop at the same time. Who goes first?

options.text: The driver on your left.
You.
Whoever is signaling to turn.

questions.explanation: When two vehicles reach a four-way stop at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: You are entering the highway on a short ramp with no acceleration lane. What should you do?

options.text: Enter the far right lane immediately and speed up to match traffic.
Use the shoulder to speed up to match traffic.
Speed up only after you find a gap in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up only after you find a gap in traffic.
questions.explanation: On a short entrance ramp with no acceleration lane, wait for a gap in traffic before speeding up and entering. Usually, you should stay stopped while waiting for a safe gap to appear.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Press hard on the brake.
Hold the steering wheel tight and use the brakes gently.
Pull over quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tight and use the brakes gently.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel tightly and keep the car straight. Slow down gradually by taking your foot off the gas and using light braking. Do not stop on the road. Pull off safely when possible.

questions.question: Your wheels drift off the edge of the pavement. What is the first thing you should do?

options.text: Turn the wheels slightly left to get back on the road.
Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas, and brake gently.
Brake hard and turn the wheels sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas, and brake gently.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle leaves the road, grip the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and apply the brakes gently. Wait until you slow down, check traffic, and find a safe place to return to the road. Jerking the wheel sharply can cause you to lose control or enter another lane.

questions.question: You must give the right-of-way to pedestrians who are:

options.text: In a marked crosswalk.
In any crosswalk or intersection.
Crossing any street.

questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians crossing in any marked or unmarked crosswalk. For safety, you should yield to anyone crossing the street.

questions.question: When is the road most slippery?

options.text: After several hours of rain.
When rain first starts.
After one to two hours of rain.

questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery when it first starts to rain. Dirt and oil mix with the water to create a slick coating on the pavement.

questions.question: Streets and highways are most slippery:

options.text: After heavy rain for several hours.
When they are clean and dry.
Just after rain starts.

questions.explanation: The first half hour of rain is dangerous because water mixes with oil and chemicals on the road that have not washed away yet. Drive slowly and carefully on slippery roads.

questions.question: If dust or smoke makes it hard to see other vehicles, you should drive slowly and turn on your:

options.text: Emergency flashers.
Parking lights.
Headlights.

questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights whenever you cannot see other vehicles. Other drivers may also have trouble seeing you.

questions.question: Oncoming vehicles are on your left and parked cars are on your right. Which way should you steer?

options.text: Closer to the oncoming vehicles.
Closer to the parked vehicles.
Down the middle between them.

questions.explanation: With oncoming vehicles on your left and parked cars on your right, steer a middle course between both groups.

questions.question: When traffic is moving at 50 to 55 mph, you are least likely to have an accident if you:

options.text: Drive a few miles per hour faster than most other vehicles.
Stay within that speed range.
Drive a few miles per hour slower than most other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Drive at the same speed as other traffic (as long as it is within the speed limit). Vehicles moving at the same speed in the same direction cannot hit each other. Crashes happen when some vehicles travel at different speeds than others.

questions.question: What does this pennant-shaped sign mean?

options.text: No passing zone.
Right turn permitted on red.
Yield right-of-way.

questions.explanation: A pennant-shaped sign marks the beginning of a no passing zone.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection with a steady yellow light and have not yet entered it. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to beat the red light.
Reduce your speed and proceed carefully through the intersection.
Come to a safe stop.

questions.explanation: At a steady yellow light, stop your vehicle safely. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through at a safe speed.

questions.question: When changing lanes, look for:

options.text: A two- to three-second gap in traffic.
A three- to four-second gap in traffic.
A four- to five-second gap in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: A four- to five-second gap in traffic.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, find a four- to five-second gap in traffic. Turn on your signal, check your blind spot, adjust your speed, and steer into the new lane. Watch for other vehicles entering the same lane.

questions.question: You want to park uphill on a two-way road with no curb. Which direction should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking uphill or downhill on a road with no curb, turn your wheels so the vehicle rolls away from the road center if the brakes fail.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at the headlights of an oncoming vehicle.
Increase your following distance.

questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous because you cannot see as well. Increase the distance between your car and the car in front to avoid a collision if they stop suddenly. Use your headlights correctly, switching between high and low beams as needed.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a road with no curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
Turn your wheels away from the edge of the road.
Keep your wheels facing straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill with no curb, turn your wheels right toward the road edge. This ensures your vehicle rolls off the road if the brakes fail.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is using its siren and flashing lights. How do you yield the right-of-way?

options.text: Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it has passed.
Stop immediately, even if you are in an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Yield to emergency vehicles with sirens and flashing lights by moving to the right edge of the road and stopping. Do not stop in an intersection. You can move again after the emergency vehicle passes.

questions.question: The best way to avoid a dangerous situation while driving is to:

options.text: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
Turn off the radio.
Always keep your eyes focused ahead of your car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always pay attention to what is happening around you—in front, to the sides, and behind. Watching your surroundings helps you see problems early and react by changing speed or position.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
Traffic signal ahead.
Railroad ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When entering a freeway, how should you check traffic?

options.text: Use your rearview and side mirrors.
Use your rearview mirror.
Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: When entering a freeway, use your side mirror and look over your shoulder. This helps you see all traffic around you before you merge.

questions.question: If you can only see 100 feet ahead due to rain, snow, dust, smoke, or fog, what is the safest speed?

options.text: 20 mph.
30 mph.
40 mph.

questions.explanation: When you can only see 100 feet ahead, do not drive faster than 30 mph. Bad weather reduces visibility, so you must slow down.

questions.question: How can you avoid hydroplaning in rain?

options.text: Drive at the speed you would use in good weather.
Apply your brakes as soon as your car starts to skid.
Slow down.

questions.explanation: When driving too fast on wet roads, your tires can lose contact with the road and slide on the water. This is called hydroplaning. The best way to prevent it is to drive slowly in rainy conditions.

questions.question: Where should your hands be on the steering wheel to turn quickly?

options.text: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
Next to each other at the top of the steering wheel.
At the top and bottom of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Place both hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel. This position is safe and lets you turn quickly when needed.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and prepare to stop if cars are coming.
Come to a complete stop, then proceed when safe.
Proceed carefully through the intersection without always stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop, then proceed when safe.
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign means stop. You must come to a complete stop and wait until it is safe to go. Stop at the marked line, or before the crosswalk, or before the intersection where you can see oncoming traffic.
